PSA for anyone considering June Homes in NYC
My SO Jasmin Tran and I used June Homes for a long term sublet from January to November. While the apartment wasn’t in the best shape, the sublet allowed us to extend our 5 years in NYC before we moved back to be closer to our families.
In the beginning of September, we discovered rats in our apartments. We immediately filed a ticket with Junes Homes and escalated. June Homes took weeks to send an exterminator to our place, and after the exterminator plugged up several massive holes behind the stove and dishwasher, he told us that the wall structure was too thin and that rats could make new holes within a day. He said as long as the walls weren’t fixed, the root issue of the rats would remain.
We brought this up with June Homes and June Homes feigned ignorance before finally sending the SAME exterminator back to our apartment. The exterminator reconfirmed his findings, and we followed up with June Homes yet again. June Homes then proceeded to try to deflect the issue to the building management and management sent their own exterminator who just unsealed and resealed the same holes. After over a month of us escalating the issue, June Homes finally sent an inspector to check the walls. The inspector confirmed the walls were inadequate and that they couldn’t be fixed while we lived here.
June Homes then tried to offer us relocation to a different apartment even though we only had a month left on the sublet lease. They finally gave us a one-time $500 rent credit (despite rent being ~4000 a month) and closed the ticket.
During this whole time, we’ve had to deal with rats tearing open our sealed food and leaving their droppings. We’ve had to sleep over at multiple friend’s places as the living conditions have been too disgusting for us to be comfortable to be inside our own place.
This is by far the worst housing experience we’ve ever had and we regret getting this sublet so much. Please be careful when subletting with them!!!
Attached are email screenshots from the ticket + pics/vids of some of our torn food and the rat droppings left behind

Side hip pain at night usually isn't your hip joint. 
If the side of your hip aches when you lie on it, the cause is often the tendons on the outside of the hip (often labeled "hip bursitis"), not arthritis.
• Joint arthritis tends to ache in the groin. Tendon pain sits on the side of the hip.
• Lying on that side, or letting your top knee drop across, squeezes the tendon against the bone.
• Stretching your knee across your body can add more squeeze. Complete rest alone lets the muscles weaken.
• In the 2018 LEAP trial (BMJ), education plus exercise beat a steroid shot at 8 weeks, and the benefit held at one year.
 Try tonight: sleep on your good side with a pillow between your knees.
Calm the squeeze, load the muscles gradually, and give it a few weeks. Results vary, so get checked if it isn't improving.

Her mother burned in front of her eyes...
Gaza massacre | October 2026
One of the days known as "Ceasefire"
The dawn was about to break into Gaza City when the occupation planes decided to turn the house of the Awad family into a mass of flames and smoke.
In moments, the fire ignited, and the house that was sheltering the family turned into a mass of flames and smoke,
The mother and her daughter came out between the martyrs and the wounded, and the mother and her daughter remained inside.
They went searching for them among the rubble and fire, until they heard the sound of a child screaming.
They approached the source of the sound, and found the scene that I don't know how humans can endure.
The child was sitting on her bed.
She wasn't running towards the door, nor searching for a window, nor trying to escape.
She was staring at her mother.
Her mother who was burning in front of her eyes.
I don't know what that little girl was waiting for, whether she was waiting for her mother to rise? To extend her hand towards her, to embrace her, and tell her that everything will be alright, just like mothers do when they fear for their children?
But her mother couldn't do anything.
And the fire didn't wait.
Oh God...
How can a child understand that the fire that consumes her mother will not stop because her daughter sees it? How can a small heart comprehend that the person who was the safety for her entire life is now helpless before her eyes, unable to save himself, let alone save her?
And how can the world end for a child, while the world around her continues on its normal day?
I don't know if the child survived her body from the fire, but I know that some scenes don't end with the moment, they remain in a place of the soul, and return in dreams, and in silence, and every time we search for a face that is absent from us.
And if this little girl is destined to grow up, what memory will she grow up with?
Will you remember her mother's embrace, her voice, and her hands as she combed her hair? Or will those memories overshadow the last dawn scene, when her mother was burning in front of her eyes, sitting on her bed, having no control over her situation?
What kind of world is this that has enough words to describe the tragedy, and enough data to condemn it, but is unable to prevent its recurrence?
They will say: a room in Gaza burned, victims fell, and then the day passes into another day.
But no one can summarize what happened in a news story.
The news will not tell you how a child sat on her bed, staring at her mother as she burned.
It will not tell you what it means to see your mother die in front of you, when you are younger than you can understand death, weaker than you can prevent it, and more in need of someone to protect you from it.
It is not just a story about a child.
This is a story of a world that saw enough to know, heard enough to move, and then left a mother burning in Gaza, and a child facing a moment that no human being should ever face.

2. Modular & Stepped Cubist Massing

Staggered Rectilinear Volumes: The tower is composed of stacked, offset block-like modules that taper as the building ascends, giving it a playful, dynamic skyline. 

Geometric Orthogonality: Straight vertical and horizontal lines govern the entire building volume, emphasizing pure geometric form. 

3. High-Contrast Material Fusion

Cladding Panels vs. Glass: Smooth colored architectural panels contrast with large window glazing and a crown glass lantern top. 

Classical Grandeur Entrance: A stepped gray stone archway framing an elegant entryway, paired with a modern chandelier and polished white marble ground pavement. 

4. Modern Landscape Integration

Inlaid Geometric Paving: The forecourt features a marble ground plane embedded with a custom Mondrian-inspired color-block mosaic. 

Organic Contrast: Pink cherry blossom (sakura) trees flank the entrance, providing a soft, natural color and organic texture that balances the rigid geometric lines of the building.

The core architectural and artistic concepts integrated into the hotel design:

1. De Stijl & Piet Mondrian Aesthetic

Primary Color Palette: The facade prominently uses the primary colors—red, yellow, and blue—balanced against neutral background colors of white, black, and gray. 

Asymmetrical Grid Layout: Rectangular planes and solid blocks are arranged within a black grid matrix, translating Piet Mondrian’s famous abstract paintings (Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow) into a three-dimensional building facade. 

2. Modernism & Brutalism

Raw Concrete Elements: Exposed raw concrete frames, beams, and cantilevered balcony boxes give the design a raw, modern structural character reminiscent of Brutalist architecture. 

Industrial Black Metal Frames: Clean, straight black vertical and horizontal framing structures hold the glass curtains and panels together, emphasizing structural grid lines. 

3. Cubism & Modular Volumetric Architecture

Cantilevered Modules: Interlocking, offset box modules project outward from the core tower, creating dynamic spatial depth, outdoor terraces, and distinct floor plans. 

Geometric Abstraction: The design relies entirely on clean geometric shapes—cubes, rectangles, and right angles—without decorative ornamentation or organic curves. 

4. Modern Glass Curtain Wall Core

Central Atrium Spine: A tall, continuous vertical glass curtain wall functions as a central light shaft and visual anchor, contrasting transparent glass panels with opaque colored panels. 

Observation Tower / Crown Box: At the top of the central column sits a fully glazed, elevated observation box/sky-lounge offering panoramic views. 

5. Geometric Formal Landscaping

Symmetrical Courtyard Layout: The ground level incorporates a structured plaza featuring neatly pruned cubical trees, paved geometric pathways, and flowering trees, extending the grid philosophy into the outdoor landscape.

You can't isolate your VMO 
 Here's what to train instead.
That teardrop muscle above your kneecap gets blamed for a lot of knee pain. But:
 One nerve, the femoral nerve, powers all four quad muscles at once
 Research going back to the 1990s couldn't find an exercise that works the VMO alone
 Toes-out leg raises and ball squeezes aren't bad, they're just too light and skip your hip
 Your gluteus medius on the side of your hip decides where your knee points
 Try this at home: chair sit-to-stands (2×10), slow step-downs off a low step (2×8 per leg), side-lying leg raises (2×12 each side). Stop if you feel sharp pain, swelling, or your knee giving way. Results vary, so check with your provider before starting something new.

Stop stretching that bent finger. It's not a tendon. 
That curl in your ring or pinky finger has a name: Dupuytren's contracture, the "Viking disease."
 The problem is the palmar fascia, a thin sheet of tissue under your palm's skin, not the tendons.
 It thickens into lumps (nodules), then cords that slowly pull the finger toward the palm.
 A 2023 study of more than 650,000 people found three of its genetic risk factors came from Neanderthals.
 Stretching won't undo a cord. The tabletop test is your early check.
 Try this: lay your hand flat on a table, palm down. If your palm and fingers can't lie flat, see a hand surgeon. After treatment, hand therapy helps you keep the straightening. Results vary.

Primary Color Palette: The building prominently uses red, blue, and yellow primary color panels set against neutral black, white, and gray surfaces. 

Geometric Grid Patterns: The exterior glass facades, ground plaza floor tiles, and window compositions follow a strict orthogonal grid layout consisting of thick black lines framing rectangular geometric color blocks. 

2. Brutalist & Modular Architecture

Raw Exposed Concrete Elements: The upper structural cantilevered frames and central balcony column feature exposed gray board-formed concrete textures. 

Cantilevered Modular Boxes: Near the top of the tower, large concrete box-like balcony modules protrude outward from the central core, giving it a sculptural, cubist profile. 

3. Modern Glass Tower & Dynamic Composition

Curtain Wall Facade: The central tower utilizes full-height glass panels that balance transparency with opaque colored grid accents. 

Glass Crown Cap: The top of the building is finished with a transparent glass cube skylight structure. 

Integrated Landscape Design: The Mondrian-inspired geometric grid layout extends into the plaza ground paving, fountains, and symmetrical landscaping surrounding the hotel entrance.

So I built **UnlistedRooms** to make that easier

It brings housing posts into one searchable place, so you can filter by things like rent, neighborhood, move-in date, duration, furnished/unfurnished, etc. You can also see people who are actively looking for housing, use the map view, and save listings you want to come back to.

When you find something interesting, the site links you back to the **original Facebook post** — it’s meant to make discovery easier, not replace the groups themselves.

It’s currently most useful for Newport, though there are Manhattan listings as well.

I built this as a personal project because I thought it would be useful for anyone going through the same housing search chaos. Would genuinely love feedback — especially if something is confusing, a filter is missing, or there’s something that would make it more useful.

Hope it helps someone here!

The core concepts and design movements used to construct this hotel concept include:

1. Piet Mondrian & De Stijl Movement (Neoplasticism)

The most prominent influence is the De Stijl movement, spearheaded by Dutch painter Piet Mondrian. 

Primary Color Palette: The facade and paving utilize the signature primary colors—red, yellow, and blue—set against neutral shades of white and gray. 

Orthogonal Grid System: Thick black structural frames form a rigid vertical and horizontal grid, subdividing the building elevation into rectangular color blocks and glass panes. 

Asymmetrical Balance: The distribution of colors and solid vs. transparent panels is non-repeating and asymmetrical, creating visual dynamism while maintaining overall harmony. 

2. Modular Structural Frame & Cubism

Exposed Black Steel Skeleton: The dark, clean structural lines frame each volume, giving the building a modular, "assembled" look reminiscent of modern container/cube architecture. 

Cantilevered Rectangular Blocks: Interlocking rectangular volumes step forward and back, creating subtle depth, shadows, and outdoor balcony spaces within the grid. 

3. Integrated Atrium & Vertical Light Art

Central Glass Atrium Column: A full-height, transparent central spine acts as a vertical light shaft, running up the center of the building. 

Kinetic Light Installation: Suspended within the central shaft is a multi-story, cascading geometric light fixture featuring miniature colored cubic pendants that mirror the Mondrian motif on the facade. 

4. Modern High-End Hospitality & Transparency

Floor-to-Ceiling Glazing: Large glass curtain walls maximize natural lighting, urban views, and interior transparency. 

Integrated Landscaping & Paving: The geometric Mondrian motif continues seamlessly onto the ground floor marble plaza layout, integrating outdoor lounge furniture, landscaping, and seasonal cherry blossom (Sakura) trees to soften the sharp geometric lines.

The hotel is heavily inspired by De Stijl (The Style) and the artistic principles of Piet Mondrian (Neo-Plasticism). 

Here are the primary architectural and design concepts used:

1. Neo-Plasticism (Piet Mondrian's Aesthetic)

Primary Color Palette: The exterior facade and interior accents rely almost exclusively on the three primary colors—Red, Blue, and Yellow—complemented by non-colors (White, Gray, and Black). 

Black Orthogonal Grid Lines: Strong, bold vertical and horizontal black lines frame the geometric panels, creating structural grid divisions across the entire facade. 

Asymmetrical Balance: The composition avoids traditional symmetry; instead, visual equilibrium is achieved by balancing blocks of primary colors and transparent glass panels of varying sizes across the tower. 

2. De Stijl Movement Principles

Pure Geometry & Abstraction: The building strips away ornamental detailing in favor of clean, rectangular forms, sharp angles, and planar surfaces. 

Integration of Art and Architecture: The artwork isn't just displayed on or inside the structure—the entire building acts as a 3D canvas. This extends to the floor graphic on the driveway and the interior lobby features, creating a cohesive experience from arrival to exterior design. 

3. 3D Modular Stacking & Cubism

Volumetric Cantilevers: Rather than being a flat 2D painting, the concept translates Mondrian's grid into a three-dimensional skyscraper by stepping, extruding, and offsetting rectangular modules, balconies, and floor plates. 

Transparency vs. Opacity: The design alternates solid opaque color panels with large floor-to-ceiling glass windows and grid curtain walls, playing with depth, light, and interior visibility.

 A higher maintenance fee doesn't always mean a better choice, just as a lower maintenance fee doesn't always mean better value.
The reason maintenance fees vary from one condo to another is usually because of differences in
 the facilities provided, the size of the building, and the amount of common area. In some cases, developers may also have different approaches to setting maintenance fees.
That's why, instead of focusing only on how much the maintenance fee is per square meter, it's more important to look at what you're getting in return, such as the facilities and the overall quality of the property's management.

Several core architectural and design concepts define the structure: 

1. Bauhaus Architectural Principles

Form Follows Function: The layout clearly expresses functional zones through distinct volumetric blocks—such as the open glass entrance lobby, podium base, main hotel room tower, cantilevered suites/amenity levels, and a illuminated top lantern pavilion. 

Minimalism & Geometry: Emphasis on clean vertical and horizontal lines, strong right angles, and unadorned structural forms. 

Honesty of Materials: Direct contrast and harmonious integration between large glass curtain walls and solid smooth light grey/white concrete facade panels. 

2. Modernist Stacking & Cantilevering

Interlocking Volumetric Blocks: Instead of a single uniform monolithic shaft, the tower uses stacked modular masses offset at different intervals. 

Cantilevered Floating Elements: Upper sections extend outward beyond the lower structural plane, creating dramatic overhangs, outdoor terrace spaces, and dynamic structural interplay. 

3. Transparency & Light Integration

Floor-to-Ceiling Glass Glazing: Maximizes natural light and city views for occupants while creating transparency at the street-level base. 

Illuminated Crown / Lantern Top: The top floors form a glass "light-box" or crown, acting as a beacon in the skyline during dusk and night. 

Warm Interior Contrast: Warm, golden interior lighting contrasts visually with the cool exterior dusk atmosphere and grey concrete. 

4. Modern Artistic Motifs

Embossed Bas-Relief Relief: A prominent crescent-moon profile face is embedded directly into the side concrete facade wall, serving as a subtle artistic logo and thematic centerpiece. 

5. Site & Landscape Integration

Water Features & Reflecting Pools: Smooth surrounding reflecting pools at the base mirror the building's geometry and enhance the sense of tranquility and luxury. 

Symmetrical Approach: A defined central pathway leads visitors across the water feature straight into the double-height glazed atrium entrance.

The core architectural and artistic concepts used to create this hotel include:

1. De Stijl & Piet Mondrian Neo-Plasticism

Primary Color Palette: Strict adherence to the primary colors—red, yellow, and blue—accented with neutrals (white, gray, black).

Orthogonal Grid System: Use of sharp rectilinear lines, horizontal and vertical black framing, and asymmetrical geometric grids across the main facade, upper cantilevered blocks, top crown, and ground paving.

Planar & Volumetric Composition: Translating 2D Mondrian canvas compositions into 3D architectural volumes, where solid colored planes intersect transparent glass facades and recessed balconies.

2. Bauhaus Functionalism & Structural Clarity

Form Follows Function: Clean geometry, exposed structural framing, and clear demarcation between base, shaft, and crown.

Industrial & Modernist Materials: High contrast combination of smooth white stone/concrete, dark metal structural frames, rectangular glass curtain walls, and solid composite panels.

Open Modernist Geometry: Clean right angles, structural grid grids, and integrated functional elements like minimalist perimeter lighting posts and metal balustrades.

3. Architectural Articulation & Dynamic Massing

Cantilevered Accent Cubes: Floating colored volumes jutting out from the central shaft, breaking the uniform tower profile and creating visual depth.

Layered Base-Tower-Crown Triad:

Base: A solid, graphic podium featuring a prominent framed grand entrance portal and geometric paving.

Mid-section (Shaft): Vertical hotel room balconies with asymmetric accent pods.

Crown: Open-frame top pavilion featuring multi-tier cantilevered roof slabs and exposed minimalist geometric chandeliers.

4. Geometric Landscape Integration

Hardscape Patterning: Extending the interior/facade De Stijl grid pattern onto the outer plazas and entrance walkways.

Biophilic Contrast: Juxtaposing the rigid, mathematical rectilinear building lines with soft natural elements (cherry blossom trees and sculpted greenery) to frame the modern entrance.
